title: Barcelona, May 2024
summary: Five-night trip focused on food, architecture and neighbourhood walks. The city was enjoyable, but crowd levels and timed reservations affected spontaneity.
whatWorked: Eixample was a practical base with good transit and easy walking routes.
Early evening walks, markets and casual restaurants were the best parts of the trip.
Mild weather made long walking days comfortable.
Having one reserved attraction per day worked better than packing the schedule.
whatDidNotWork: The busiest attractions required more advance planning than preferred.
Crowds around major sights reduced enjoyment.
Moving between beach, old town and hill viewpoints in one day made the day feel fragmented.
weatherNotes: Comfortable around 21-25C. Direct sun felt tiring by mid-afternoon, so shaded routes and breaks were useful.
futureRecommendation: Barcelona is a good fit in shoulder season if the plan limits major attractions and leaves evenings open for food, walking and neighbourhood exploration.
